1.why: Headings and body text use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line spacing, although letter spacing is default rather than notably generous.

2.why: All instructional text appears in sentence case with no italics, all-caps, or dense paragraph blocks on any screen.

3.why: The single-column centred card with large inputs and short text lines should remain readable at phone width, though only desktop-width renders were observed.

4.why: Instructions are one or two short plain sentences (e.g., 'Confirm your mobile number.'), though jargon such as 'MFA' and 'setup secret' remains.

5.why: Example placeholders are shown for the mobile number (+15551234567) and recovery code (ABCD-EFGH-IJKL) fields, but the verification-code and authenticator-code fields show no example.

6.why: The user must read the growing dense monospace Logs panel to proceed, because the verification code and current OTP are delivered only inside that block.

7.why: No copy button is provided anywhere and step 4 explicitly says to 'add it manually to your authenticator app', so secrets and codes are expected to be typed by hand.

8.why: Only manual entry of the setup secret is offered; no QR code or equivalent alternative appears at any step.

9.why: The login uses standard email/password inputs that password managers can usually fill, but nothing observable in the screenshots confirms deliberate autofill or one-time-code support.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading naming the step and a visually dominant blue primary button, though the settings screen shows three competing buttons.

11.why: Most screens request a single action, but the verify screen shows 'Send verification code' and 'Verify identity' together and the settings screen presents verify, regenerate, and log out at once.

12.why: Some outcomes are stated plainly ('Recovery code accepted and used.'), but after requesting a code the only feedback is a log entry and a newly appearing field rather than an explicit statement of what happened and what comes next.

13.why: The user can re-request the verification code, retry after the generic error, and regenerate recovery codes without penalty, but no reveal/hide toggle exists for the password or codes.

14.why: The error 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' is non-blaming but does not state what the problem was or how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown, reading timeout, or session-expiry warning appears on any screen, so the user can read and enter codes at their own pace.
